sender.en: A new online match or social media admirer

name.en: Romance scam: an online love who needs money or wants you to invest

how.en: Someone you meet on a dating app or social media builds a close relationship, chatting several times a day, and soon asks to move to another app. They always have a reason not to meet in person: work far away, a job abroad or the military. Then they ask for money for an emergency, a flight to visit you or surgery, or offer to teach you to invest in crypto or stocks on a platform they choose. Nearly 60% of people who reported losing money to a romance scam in 2025 said it started on social media.

text.en: Someone you met online gets close fast and wants to chat on another app.
They always have a reason they can’t meet in person or video call.
They ask for money for an emergency, a trip to see you or a medical bill.
Or they offer to coach you to invest in crypto on a site that shows big profits.

Good morning my love. I can’t stop thinking about you. As soon as my contract on the oil rig ends we will finally be together. Baby, my account is frozen and I need help with the customs fee to send my things home. I will pay you back as soon as I land.

en: An online love you have never met in person asks for money.
Excuses for never meeting or video calling.
Investment tips or “coaching” from a love interest.
Requests for gift cards, wire transfers or crypto.
Never send money or gifts to someone you haven’t met in person.
Never let someone you met online direct your investment decisions.
Do a reverse image search of their photos, and talk to a friend or relative you trust.
Report the profile to the app or site, and ask the company you used to pay if the money can be recovered.
